tasks.goal: a Node log-summary tool built from three .mjs files in the workspace. (1) lib/parse.mjs exports parseLine(line) returning {ts, level, message} for a line shaped '<ISO-timestamp> <LEVEL> <message>' and null for any line that does not match; it imports nothing. (2) lib/render.mjs exports renderTable(rows) taking an array of [label, value] pairs and returning a plain-text two-column table string whose labels are left-aligned and padded to the widest label; it imports nothing. (3) summarize.mjs is the command-line entry point: it reads a log file path from argv[2], turns every line into an entry with parseLine, counts the entries per level, and prints those counts through renderTable — one row per level sorted alphabetically plus a final TOTAL row — exiting 1 with a clear stderr message when the path is missing or unreadable. lib/parse.mjs and lib/render.mjs know nothing about each other: neither imports the other, they share no file, and each one is fully specified by the contract above. Each of the two library files ships a self-check beside it (lib/parse.check.mjs, lib/render.check.mjs) exercising its exported function against inline sample data and exiting non-zero on a mismatch. Ship fixtures/sample.log for the entry point and a README.md whose 'Verified invocations' section documents the real observed output of every command that was actually run.

a Node CSV column-report tool built from three .mjs files in the workspace. (1) lib/csv.mjs exports parseCsv(text) returning {headers, rows} where headers is the trimmed first line split on commas and rows is an array of arrays of trimmed cells, blank lines ignored; it imports nothing. (2) lib/stats.mjs exports computeStats(numbers) returning {count, min, max, mean} with mean rounded to two decimals, and throwing an Error with a clear message on an empty array or a non-numeric element; it imports nothing. (3) report.mjs is the command-line entry point: it reads a CSV path from argv[2] and a column name from argv[3], turns the file into a table with parseCsv, feeds that column's values to computeStats, and prints 'count=<n> min=<n> max=<n> mean=<n>', exiting 1 with a clear stderr message when the path is missing or unreadable or when the column name is not one of the headers. lib/csv.mjs and lib/stats.mjs know nothing about each other: neither imports the other, they share no file, and each one is fully specified by the contract above. Each of the two library files ships a self-check beside it (lib/csv.check.mjs, lib/stats.check.mjs) exercising its exported function against inline sample data — including the error cases — and exiting non-zero on a mismatch. Ship fixtures/sample.csv for the entry point and a README.md whose 'Verified invocations' section documents the real observed output of every command that was actually run.

a Node markdown table-of-contents tool built from three .mjs files in the workspace. (1) lib/headings.mjs exports extractHeadings(markdown) returning an array of {level, text} for every ATX heading, ignoring any heading inside a fenced code block; it imports nothing. (2) lib/slug.mjs exports slugify(text) returning the GitHub-style anchor of a heading: lowercased, spaces turned into single hyphens, characters other than letters, digits and hyphens dropped; it imports nothing. (3) toc.mjs is the command-line entry point: it reads a markdown file path from argv[2], collects its headings with extractHeadings, and prints one line per heading as '- [<text>](#<slug>)' indented by two spaces per level below the first, exiting 1 with a clear stderr message when the path is missing or unreadable. lib/headings.mjs and lib/slug.mjs know nothing about each other: neither imports the other, they share no file, and each one is fully specified by the contract above. Each of the two library files ships a self-check beside it (lib/headings.check.mjs, lib/slug.check.mjs) exercising its exported function against inline sample data and exiting non-zero on a mismatch. Ship fixtures/sample.md — including a fenced code block containing a '#' line — for the entry point, and a README.md whose 'Verified invocations' section documents the real observed output of every command that was actually run.

a zero-dependency Node HTTP task API built from three .mjs files in the workspace. (1) lib/validate.mjs exports validateTask(obj) returning {ok, errors} where errors lists a message for each violated rule: title must be a non-empty string, done must be a boolean when present; it imports nothing. (2) lib/store.mjs exports createStore() returning an in-memory store object with add(task) assigning an incrementing numeric id and returning the stored task, list() returning every stored task, get(id) returning the task or undefined, and remove(id) returning true or false; it imports nothing. (3) server.mjs is the entry point: it wires both libraries into an HTTP service binding the port in process.env.PORT (accepting 0) and printing LISTENING_ON_PORT=<n> once ready, serving GET /tasks (200, the list as JSON), POST /tasks (201 with the stored task, or 400 with {"errors":[...]} when validateTask rejects the body), GET /tasks/:id (200 or 404) and DELETE /tasks/:id (204 or 404). lib/validate.mjs and lib/store.mjs know nothing about each other: neither imports the other, they share no file, and each one is fully specified by the contract above. Each of the two library files ships a self-check beside it (lib/validate.check.mjs, lib/store.check.mjs) exercising its exported function against inline sample data and exiting non-zero on a mismatch. Ship a README.md whose 'Verified invocations' section documents the real observed status codes and bodies of every request that was actually issued.

three UNRELATED command-line utilities plus one catalog that runs them all. Each utility lives in its OWN subdirectory, shares no code and no file with the other two, and is fully specified on its own: (1) tools/rot13/index.mjs — reads a text file path from argv[2] and prints its ROT13 transform, exiting 1 with a clear stderr message on a missing or unreadable path, shipping its own tools/rot13/fixture.txt; (2) tools/wordfreq/index.mjs — reads a text file path from argv[2] and prints the three most frequent words as '<word> <count>' lines, ties broken alphabetically, exiting 1 with a clear stderr message on a missing or unreadable path, shipping its own tools/wordfreq/fixture.txt; (3) tools/hexdump/index.mjs — reads a file path from argv[2] and prints its first 32 bytes as space-separated lowercase hex, exiting 1 with a clear stderr message on a missing or unreadable path, shipping its own tools/hexdump/fixture.bin. The three utilities have nothing in common: no shared module, no shared fixture, no shared directory, and none of them imports another. Once they exist, catalog.mjs at the workspace root invokes each utility as a child process against that utility's own fixture and prints one line per utility as '<name> exit=<code> first=<first line of its stdout>', in alphabetical order of name, exiting 1 when any utility exits non-zero. Ship a README.md whose 'Verified invocations' section documents the real observed output of every command that was actually run, including catalog.mjs.

three UNRELATED data files produced by three independent generators, plus one digest that consumes all three. Each generator lives in its OWN subdirectory, shares no code and no file with the other two, and is fully specified on its own: (1) gen/primes/index.mjs — writes gen/primes/out.json containing {"kind":"primes","values":[...]} with every prime below 200; (2) gen/fib/index.mjs — writes gen/fib/out.json containing {"kind":"fib","values":[...]} with the first 25 Fibonacci numbers starting at 1, 1; (3) gen/squares/index.mjs — writes gen/squares/out.json containing {"kind":"squares","values":[...]} with the squares of 1 through 30. Each generator prints '<kind>: <n> values' to stdout and exits 0. The three generators have nothing in common: no shared module, no shared output file, no shared directory, and none of them imports another. Once the three out.json files exist, digest.mjs at the workspace root reads all three — under the base directory given as argv[2], defaulting to '.' — and prints one line per kind as '<kind> count=<n> min=<n> max=<n> sum=<n>' in alphabetical order of kind, then a final 'TOTAL count=<n> sum=<n>' line; given a base directory that holds no such files it exits 1 with a clear stderr message naming the first one it could not read. Ship a README.md whose 'Verified invocations' section documents the real observed output of every command that was actually run, including digest.mjs.
